prompt: HBr adds to 1,3-butadiene at 0 °C. What percent of the product mixture is the 1,2 adduct?
explanation: At 0 °C the reaction gives a 71 : 29 mixture of 1,2 and 1,4 adducts. Under these kinetically controlled conditions, the more rapidly formed 1,2 adduct predominates.

prompt: HBr adds to 1,3-butadiene at 40 °C. What percent of the product mixture is the 1,4 adduct?
explanation: At 40 °C the same reaction gives a 15 : 85 mixture of 1,2 and 1,4 adducts. The reaction is under thermodynamic control, so the more stable 1,4 adduct predominates.

prompt: The 1,4 adduct makes up 29% of the HBr + 1,3-butadiene product at 0 °C and 85% at 40 °C. By how many percentage points does its share rise?
explanation: 85 − 29 = 56 percentage points. Raising the temperature from 0 °C to 40 °C switches the reaction from kinetic to thermodynamic control, and the more stable 1,4 adduct takes over.

prompt: At 40 °C, HBr and 1,3-butadiene give a 15 : 85 mixture of 1,2 and 1,4 adducts. How many times as much 1,4 adduct as 1,2 adduct is formed, to two decimal places?
explanation: 85 ÷ 15 = 5.67. At equilibrium the more stable 1,4 adduct outnumbers the 1,2 adduct by more than five to one.

prompt: Adding HBr to 1,3-butadiene at 0 °C gives 20.0 g of bromobutenes. Using the 71 : 29 ratio of 1,2 to 1,4 adducts, how many grams of 3-bromo-1-butene form?
explanation: 3-Bromo-1-butene is the 1,2 adduct, 71% of the mixture at 0 °C: 0.71 × 20.0 g = 14.2 g. The remaining 5.8 g is 1-bromo-2-butene.

prompt: What is meant by kinetic control of a reaction?

choices.text: The reaction is irreversible, so the product that forms faster predominates
The reaction is reversible, so the more stable product predominates
choices.why: That is thermodynamic (equilibrium) control.

choices.text: The reaction is irreversible, so the more stable product predominates
choices.why: Without equilibrium, stability doesn't matter. The product of an irreversible reaction depends only on relative rates.

choices.text: The products reach equilibrium, so the faster-forming product predominates
choices.why: Once products are in equilibrium, the more stable one predominates regardless of rate. Kinetic control means no equilibrium is reached.

explanation: When both processes are irreversible (typically at lower temperature), no equilibrium is reached and the product that forms faster is the major one. The product of an irreversible reaction depends only on relative rates, not on stability; such reactions are under kinetic control.

prompt: In the addition of HBr to 1,3-butadiene, which compound is the kinetic product?

choices.text: 3-Bromo-1-butene, the 1,2 adduct
1-Bromo-2-butene, the 1,4 adduct
choices.why: The 1,4 adduct is the thermodynamic product: more stable, but formed more slowly.

choices.text: 4-Bromo-1-butene, from the primary carbocation
choices.why: The primary nonallylic carbocation doesn't form. The two products are 3-bromo-1-butene and 1-bromo-2-butene.

choices.text: Whichever adduct is more stable
choices.why: The kinetic product is the one that forms faster; here that is the less stable 1,2 adduct.

explanation: The 1,2 adduct, 3-bromo-1-butene, is the kinetic product because it forms faster; it predominates at 0 °C (71 : 29). The 1,4 adduct, 1-bromo-2-butene, is the thermodynamic product because it is more stable (Figure 14.3.2).

prompt: Why is 1-bromo-2-butene called the thermodynamic product of HBr addition to 1,3-butadiene?

choices.text: It is the more stable adduct, so it predominates once the products equilibrate
It forms faster than the 1,2 adduct
choices.why: The 1,2 adduct forms faster. The 1,4 adduct wins only under equilibrium conditions.

choices.text: It is the only product formed at 40 °C
choices.why: At 40 °C it is the major product (85%), but 15% of the 1,2 adduct is still present.

choices.text: It predominates at low temperature, where the reactions are irreversible
choices.why: At low temperature (0 °C) the faster-forming 1,2 adduct predominates. The 1,4 adduct predominates at higher temperature.

explanation: 1-Bromo-2-butene, the 1,4 adduct, is more stable than the 1,2 adduct. At 40 °C the addition becomes reversible and an equilibrium mixture (15 : 85) results, in which the more stable 1,4 adduct predominates.

prompt: Why does the 1,4 adduct predominate when HBr adds to 1,3-butadiene at 40 °C instead of 0 °C?

choices.text: The higher temperature lets the addition become reversible, so an equilibrium mixture forms
The higher temperature makes the 1,4 adduct form faster than the 1,2 adduct
choices.why: The 1,2 adduct still forms faster. The change comes from equilibration, which favors the more stable 1,4 adduct.

choices.text: The higher temperature makes the 1,2 adduct the more stable product
choices.why: The 1,4 adduct is the more stable product at either temperature. Temperature changes whether equilibrium is reached.

choices.text: At 40 °C no allylic carbocation forms, so only 1,4-addition can occur
choices.why: The same allylic cation forms at both temperatures; both adducts are still present at 40 °C.

explanation: At 0 °C the reaction can't reach equilibrium, so the product that forms faster (the 1,2 adduct) predominates. At 40 °C the addition process becomes reversible, an equilibrium mixture results, and the more stable 1,4 adduct predominates (15 : 85).

prompt: The product mixture formed from HBr and 1,3-butadiene at 0 °C is heated to 40 °C in the presence of HBr. What happens?

choices.text: The ratio of 1,2 to 1,4 adducts slowly changes from 71 : 29 to 15 : 85
Nothing; once formed, the adducts no longer change
choices.why: At 40 °C the adducts interconvert, so the mixture drifts to the equilibrium ratio.

choices.text: The ratio slowly changes from 15 : 85 to 71 : 29
choices.why: That's backward. The mixture starts at the kinetic ratio, 71 : 29, and moves to the equilibrium ratio, 15 : 85.

choices.text: The 1,4 adduct is slowly converted entirely into the 1,2 adduct
choices.why: The more stable 1,4 adduct grows at the higher temperature; it doesn't disappear.

explanation: When the 0 °C mixture is heated to 40 °C with HBr, the ratio slowly changes from 71 : 29 to 15 : 85. The 1,2 and 1,4 adducts interconvert at the higher temperature and reach equilibrium, where the more stable 1,4 adduct predominates.

prompt: At 40 °C, the 1,2 and 1,4 adducts of HBr and 1,3-butadiene interconvert. By what mechanism?

choices.text: S_N1 dissociation of either adduct to the same allylic carbocation
S_N2 attack of Br− on the carbon that already bears Br
choices.why: That would simply swap one Br for another and give back the same compound. Interconversion needs the shared allylic cation.

choices.text: A radical chain reaction through an allylic radical
choices.why: No radicals are involved. The adducts ionize to a common carbocation intermediate.

choices.text: Direct movement of the double bond, with no intermediate
choices.why: The adducts interconvert through an intermediate: the allylic cation that both form by losing Br−.

explanation: Either adduct can lose Br− in an S_N1 dissociation, giving the same allylic carbocation. Br− can then bond at either end of the cation, so the two adducts interconvert and reach equilibrium (Exercise 14.3.1).

prompt: Why is the 1,4 adduct of HBr and 1,3-butadiene, 1-bromo-2-butene, more stable than the 1,2 adduct, 3-bromo-1-butene?

choices.text: Its double bond is more highly substituted
Its double bond is less highly substituted
choices.why: BrCH2CH=CHCH3 has a disubstituted double bond, while CH2=CHCHBrCH3 has a monosubstituted one. More substitution means more stability.

choices.text: It has more carbon atoms
choices.why: Both adducts are C4H7Br isomers with the same atoms.

choices.text: Its double bond is at the end of the chain
choices.why: That describes the 1,2 adduct, CH2=CHCHBrCH3, whose terminal double bond is the less stable one.

explanation: In 1-bromo-2-butene, BrCH2CH=CHCH3, the double bond is disubstituted; in 3-bromo-1-butene, CH2=CHCHBrCH3, it is monosubstituted. More highly substituted double bonds are more stable (Exercise 14.3.2).

prompt: A reactant A can give product B or product C. B forms faster, but C is more stable. At a higher temperature, where both reactions are readily reversible, which product is major?

choices.text: C, because the product ratio depends only on stability
B, because the product ratio depends only on rate
choices.why: Once the products equilibrate, rate no longer matters. That rule applies under kinetic control, when the reactions are irreversible.

choices.text: Equal amounts of B and C, because both reactions are reversible
choices.why: Reversibility lets B and C reach equilibrium, and at equilibrium the more stable product predominates.

choices.text: B, because higher temperature speeds up only the faster reaction
choices.why: Higher temperature makes both processes reversible, and the more stable product, C, predominates.

explanation: At higher temperature both processes are readily reversible and reach equilibrium. Because C is more stable, it is the major product even though it forms more slowly. The product of a readily reversible reaction depends only on stability: equilibrium (thermodynamic) control.

prompt: In electrophilic additions to conjugated dienes, which adduct normally predominates at or below room temperature, and which often predominates at higher temperature?

choices.text: 1,2 adduct at or below room temperature; 1,4 adduct at higher temperature
1,4 adduct at or below room temperature; 1,2 adduct at higher temperature
choices.why: Reversed. The faster-forming 1,2 adduct wins at low temperature; the more stable 1,4 adduct often wins at higher temperature.

choices.text: 1,2 adduct at all temperatures
choices.why: At higher temperatures the product ratio often changes and the 1,4 adduct predominates.

choices.text: 1,4 adduct at all temperatures
choices.why: At or below room temperature the 1,2 adduct normally predominates.

explanation: Electrophilic addition to a conjugated diene at or below room temperature normally gives a mixture in which the 1,2 adduct predominates. At higher temperatures the product ratio often changes and the 1,4 adduct predominates.

prompt: Which statement correctly compares the 1,2 and 1,4 adducts formed from HBr and 1,3-butadiene?

choices.text: The 1,2 adduct forms over a lower energy barrier, but the 1,4 adduct is lower in energy
The 1,4 adduct forms over a lower energy barrier and is also lower in energy
choices.why: Then the 1,4 adduct would win at every temperature. In fact the 1,2 adduct forms faster, so its barrier is lower.

choices.text: The 1,2 adduct forms over a lower energy barrier and is also lower in energy
choices.why: The 1,2 adduct forms faster, but the 1,4 adduct is the more stable product.

choices.text: The 1,4 adduct forms over a lower energy barrier, but the 1,2 adduct is lower in energy
choices.why: That's reversed: the 1,2 adduct is the kinetic product (faster) and the 1,4 adduct is the thermodynamic product (more stable).

explanation: The 1,2 adduct is the kinetic product because it forms faster, so the barrier to forming it (ΔG‡) is smaller. The 1,4 adduct is the thermodynamic product because it is more stable, so it lies lower in energy (Figure 14.3.2).
